extracted.intended_audience: press officers, science communicators, journal/publicity teams and journalists writing clinical trial press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting press releases about randomized clinical trials so they comply with CONSORT reporting standards and accurately represent trial methods, results, limitations, and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify as randomized trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly identify the study as a randomized trial in the title/abstract or lead of the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear up front that the study is a randomized trial (not observational). Avoid wording that obscures trial design. Common violation: presenting trial findings as general observational results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a structured summary (title/abstract style) covering key trial elements in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise, structured lead that covers design, participants, interventions, primary outcomes, main results, and conclusions. This mirrors CONSORT's emphasis on a structured abstract to convey essential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial design
rubrics_metrics.description: State the trial design (e.g., parallel, factorial, cluster) used in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify whether the trial was parallel-group, crossover, factorial, cluster-randomized, etc., since design affects interpretation and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Report key eligibility criteria for participants (inclusion/exclusion) so readers understand who was studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize main inclusion and exclusion criteria (age ranges, disease severity, comorbidities) rather than long lists. Omitting eligibility can lead to inappropriate generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions and comparator
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the interventions tested and the comparator with sufficient detail for readers to understand what was compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify dose, delivery, frequency, and what the comparator was (placebo, standard care, alternative treatment). Make clear which arm is the intervention and which is control/comparator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (primary and secondary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the primary outcome(s) and key secondary outcomes that the trial was designed to assess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify the prespecified primary outcome(s). Report whether results presented are for primary or secondary outcomes and caution readers when emphasizing secondary or exploratory endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the planned and/or actual sample size for the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the number of participants the trial aimed to enroll (sample size calculation) and the number actually enrolled/analyzed. Note if the study was underpowered or had sample size deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization method
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how participants were randomized (method, allocation ratio, stratification if used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide brief details about sequence generation and allocation approach (e.g., computer-generated randomization, 1:1 allocation). This affects bias risk; lack of randomization details reduces interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (masking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report who was blinded (participants, clinicians, outcome assessors) and whether blinding was successful or feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate if the trial was double-blind, single-blind, open-label, or had blinded outcome assessment. If blinding was not possible, explain potential impacts on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant flow (CONSORT diagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide participant flow information (numbers randomized, received intervention, lost to follow-up, analyzed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the CONSORT flow (how many assessed, randomized, followed, and analyzed). If possible, include or link to the CONSORT diagram. Omitting flow information obscures attrition and per-protocol vs intention-to-treat analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment dates
rubrics_metrics.description: State the recruitment period/dates during which participants were enrolled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide start and end dates (or at least years) for recruitment to help contextualize applicability and contemporaneity of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline data
rubrics_metrics.description: Report key baseline characteristics of participants to show comparability between groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize main baseline demographics and clinical characteristics (age, sex, disease severity) and note any important imbalances that could affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers analyzed
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the denominator used for analyses (how many participants were included in each analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether analyses were intention-to-treat, per-protocol, or modified intention-to-treat, and provide counts for each analysis set. Avoid ambiguity about denominators when reporting effect sizes or percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the trial outcomes with quantitative estimates of effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measured outcome values and the estimated effect size (difference, risk reduction, hazard ratio, etc.). Avoid vague summary language without numerical estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute effect sizes (report absolute numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include absolute measures of effect (e.g., absolute risk reduction, absolute event rates), not only relative measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always present absolute numbers and rates alongside relative measures. Common violation: reporting only relative risk reduction which can mislead about magnitude. Provide denominators (e.g., events per 1,000 or per-arm counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative effect sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Report relative measures of effect (e.g., relative risk, hazard ratios) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative measures can be informative but must be paired with absolute risks to avoid exaggerating perceived benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide confidence intervals for effect estimates to convey precision and uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report 95% CIs (or specified interval) for key estimates rather than p-values alone. Common violation: reporting point estimates without confidence intervals, which obscures uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harms and adverse events
rubrics_metrics.description: Report adverse events and harms observed in the trial, including frequency and severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both absolute counts and rates for harms, and specify which were serious. Omitting harms is a frequent and important violation of transparent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limitations of the trial (biases, sample size, follow-up duration, generalizability constraints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state important limitations rather than implying none. Failure to mention limitations is listed as a common violation and can lead to overinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizability (external validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe to whom the results are generalizable and any key restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the populations/settings to which the findings likely apply and those where caution is needed. Avoid broad generalizations beyond the studied population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation in context of other evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the trial findings in the context of existing evidence, including consistency or differences with prior studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare results with prior trials and systematic reviews, and avoid presenting single-trial findings as definitive. 'Single-trial findings as definitive' is a common violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration number
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the trial registration identifier (registry name and number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the registration ID (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov number) to allow readers to access protocol and pre-specified outcomes. Mention if registration was retrospective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol availability
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the trial protocol is available and where it can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to the trial protocol or publication. Protocol availability supports transparency about pre-specified outcomes and analysis plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose funding sources and role of funders in design, conduct, analysis, or reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state who funded the trial and whether funders influenced study design, data collection, analysis, or the press release. Omission of funding is a common violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish from observational findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly distinguish randomized trial evidence from observational studies when discussing causation and implication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflating RCT results with observational evidence. Make it explicit that RCTs provide different levels of evidence for causality than observational designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid causal overreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid making causal claims beyond what the trial supports, especially when reporting subgroup or secondary/exploratory findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use definitive causal language (e.g., 'cures') without appropriate evidence. Common violations include causal overreach and using 'cure' language without basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include link to full trial publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a direct link to the full trial publication (journal article or preprint) when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link readers to the peer-reviewed paper or full report so they can verify methods and results. If unavailable, indicate when/where the full report will be published.
